about: Research notes come from docs/research/landscape-brief.md and docs/research/verification-results.json (scan of 10 to 12 October 2026). Every note lists its sources.

tools.name: Claude Code (terminal)
tools.research_note: Claude Code has a screen reader mode. Turn it on by starting it with claude --ax-screen-reader, by setting the environment variable CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1, or with "axScreenReader": true in its settings file; it needs version 2.1.181 or later and was officially released on 20 July 2026. The mode prints plain labelled lines (you:, claude:, tool:, Permission Required:), turns menus into numbered lists you answer by typing a number, reads changes line by line with plus and minus before you approve them, and rings the terminal bell when a reply ends or a question waits. It does not turn on by itself when a screen reader is running, costs are announced only when you exit, and in August 2026 Anthropic confirmed that built-in speech, sound cues and heading rules are not shipped.

tools.name: Claude Code for VS Code
tools.research_note: Since version 2.1.236 (19 August 2026) the Claude Code extension for VS Code announces each reply once when it is complete, and announces permission requests, errors and status changes, with no setting needed. Each turn has a hidden heading so you can jump from turn to turn, and version 2.1.268 added the command Claude Code: Focus last message. A VoiceOver user reported on 28 September 2026 that version 2.1.283 stopped echoing typed characters (issue 97889).

tools.name: Claude Desktop (Code tab)
tools.research_note: Desktop version 1.17377 (21 July 2026) added a heading for each turn, permission requests announced without taking focus, and announcements when a response starts and ends. Still open in October 2026: the conversation list removes the message your screen reader is reading (issue 99332), the file and change panel reads every line as "Add comment" with VoiceOver (issue 100911), and NVDA users report a silent slash menu and new replies that are not announced (issues 94353 and 95937). A community script, claude-desktop-stable-feed, keeps every message loaded, but you must paste it into the developer console each time you start the app.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
tools.research_note: Codex CLI has no dedicated screen reader mode. Since 1 May 2026 it turns animations off for screen readers, and since 16 September 2026 it checks for a running screen reader when it starts and then saves the setting tui.animations=false. Version 0.154.0 made VoiceOver read fragments of output until animations were turned off (issue 44728). The request for a --screen-reader flag (issue 20489, 30 April 2026) is still open, and JAWS and VoiceOver users still reported repeated or missing speech in October.

tools.name: Codex desktop app (ChatGPT desktop)
tools.research_note: Screen reader users filed about ten accessibility issues on the Codex desktop app, now part of the ChatGPT desktop app, between April and October 2026. Reported problems include focus jumping to the top while it writes (issue 22816), a "/" suggestion menu that NVDA cannot see (issue 32375), no status announcements (issue 38246), and replies during an active task arriving with no VoiceOver announcement (issue 52784, 10 October 2026). A JAWS user reported in July that most heading problems were fixed, and a VoiceOver user on AppleVis called the Mac app the best native experience they had used with VoiceOver, though lacking features.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
tools.research_note: GitHub Copilot CLI has had a --screen-reader mode since it became generally available on 25 February 2026. Its new terminal interface, generally available on 23 June 2026, turns screen reader support on by itself when it detects a screen reader, with labelled icons and animations that switch themselves off. Version 1.0.71 (16 July 2026) announces the focused row in pickers and 1.0.81 (27 August 2026) added Ctrl+Space voice dictation. Issue 1642, filed in February by a blind developer, says the status bar is announced on every keypress and has had no reply from the maintainers.

tools.name: VS Code with GitHub Copilot Chat
tools.research_note: VS Code 1.116 (15 April 2026) added an accessibility help dialog for the Agents window, opened with Alt+F1, and landmarks. Version 1.131 (29 July 2026) added built-in offline dictation in chat, editor and terminal, and a terminal accessible view that keeps your reading position while output keeps arriving. Version 1.137 added an experimental Voice Mode for talking to an agent, for individual Copilot plans only. Still open: NVDA stops reading after file dialogs (issue 326546).

tools.name: Cursor
tools.research_note: Cursor 3.23 (early October 2026) lists accessibility fixes: screen readers announce the highlighted item and its position in the agent input's / and @ menus, and buttons in the agent chat show a focus ring when reached by keyboard. Older forum reports, whose dates could not be confirmed, describe the agent panel as "completely opaque" to NVDA and JAWS, while the editor itself works like VS Code. No Cursor accessibility statement, and no blind user confirming the 3.23 fixes, was found.

tools.name: Gemini CLI
tools.research_note: Gemini CLI has a plain-text screen reader mode: start it with --screen-reader, or set ui.accessibility.screenReader to true in its settings. A blind user called it "very usable with a screen reader", but its screen reader cursor bug was closed as not planned on 10 May 2026. On 18 June 2026 Gemini CLI stopped serving free, Google AI Pro and Ultra requests in favour of Antigravity CLI; paid API keys and Code Assist Standard and Enterprise are not affected.

tools.name: Google Antigravity CLI
tools.research_note: Antigravity CLI, which replaced Gemini CLI for free users on 18 June 2026, has no screen reader mode. The request to restore --screen-reader support (issue 6, opened 19 May 2026) is still open; a Google engineer assigned it to themselves on 20 August 2026 with no reply since. Blind users report they could not get past the first-run setup with VoiceOver and that it is "impossible for some tasks".

tools.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
tools.research_note: Cognition renamed Windsurf to Devin Desktop on 2 June 2026 and replaced its Cascade agent with Devin Local. A "Screen Reader Optimized" marketing claim could not be confirmed by any user report, test or documentation. Nothing was found about how the Devin cloud agent works with screen readers.

tools.name: Lovable
tools.research_note: Lovable's accessibility statement, last updated 6 August 2026, aims for WCAG 2.2 level AA, based on an evaluation by Funka between 23 February and 10 July 2026. It is unclear whether this covers the workspace where you build or only the marketing site, and no reports from blind people building with Lovable were found. Nothing comparable was found for Bolt, v0, Base44 or Replit.

sources.title: Lovable accessibility statement

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.research_note: OpenCode has no accessibility mode. An earlier request was closed by a stale bot on 29 April 2026 after maintainers said they had no capacity, and a detailed proposal for a screen_reader setting from a blind NVDA user (issue 39368, 28 July 2026) is still open. Users report that the desktop app hides streaming text from screen readers, and issue 54652 (12 October 2026) says version 2 still does.

tools.name: BlindPilot
tools.research_note: BlindPilot is an open source desktop app (MIT licence) that runs Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI, opencode and other agents, and splits each answer into rows you move through with the arrow keys, with narration modes, permission dialogs and sound cues. It had more than 130 tagged versions between 9 August and 11 October 2026. One person maintains it, the macOS build is not notarized, Linux is the least tested, and every agent runs in Bypass permissions mode by default, so the agent does not ask before it acts.

tools.name: agentaloud
tools.research_note: agentaloud is a Windows app, started on 2 September 2026, that runs Claude Code or Codex in the background and shows the conversation as a read-only transcript, with single-letter keys to jump between prompts, answers and tool steps. Each tool step is spoken as one sentence through NVDA, and permission requests appear as dialogs that show the exact command. It needs Windows 10 or 11 and NVDA, and how mature it is was not known in October 2026.
